summary: The Locally Led Development and Humanitarian Response Act encourages United States foreign assistance agencies to adopt a model focused on locally led development and humanitarian response. The bill directs relevant agencies to expand engagement and funding for local partners, simplify application processes, offer local language support, increase indirect cost rate thresholds, and provide periodic reports to Congress.

affected_groups.effect: They may experience increased direct funding, simplified application processes in local languages, more flexible funding modalities, and greater leadership opportunities in project design and implementation.
affected_groups.group: Local partners and actors in foreign countries

affected_groups.effect: Agency heads must initiate policy changes within 180 days to institutionalize local partner actions, conduct assessments, submit reports to Congress, and recruit or retain sufficient contracting and grant officers.
affected_groups.group: Relevant United States foreign assistance agencies and personnel

key_provisions: Directs the head of the relevant foreign assistance agency to localize the development and humanitarian assistance partner base by simplifying access to resources, offering matching grants, and engaging local actors.
Authorizes foreign assistance agencies to accept applications and proposals in languages other than English and requires an assessment of local language support options.
Allows agencies to increase the de minimis indirect cost rate by 5 percentage points for local partners receiving assistance awards or acquisitions.

Provides temporary exemptions for local entities from certain reporting requirements, permitting up to a 180-day delay in obtaining unique entity identifiers and registering in the System for Award Management.
Grants local competition authority to limit contract competition to local entities under certain conditions, capped at awards under $25 million and 10 percent of annual appropriations.
Authorizes foreign entities to use national or international generally accepted accounting principles instead of U.S. GAAP for certain contracts or grants.
Requires annual reports to Congress regarding funding amounts implemented by local partners, use of new authorities, and agency progress.
missing_information: The specific name of the relevant foreign assistance agency is not explicitly named in the text other than by definition as the department or agency primarily responsible under part I of the Foreign Assistance Act of 1961.
Specific funding amounts or appropriations authorized by the bill are not mentioned.
summary_detail.plain_summary: The Locally Led Development and Humanitarian Response Act encourages United States foreign assistance agencies to adopt a model focused on locally led development and humanitarian response. The bill directs relevant agencies to expand engagement and funding for local partners, simplify application processes, offer local language support, increase indirect cost rate thresholds, and provide periodic reports to Congress.
summary_detail.significance: The bill represents a moderate shift in how U.S. foreign assistance is structured, aiming to increase direct funding and leadership opportunities for local organizations in developing countries while granting federal agencies specific regulatory flexibilities and reporting requirements.
